item.title: RIP Billy Boston
item.description:
Billy Boston, the first Rugby League player to be awarded a Knighthood. Still regarded as one of the all time greats. When I was 14, my dad spotted him in a crowd of supporters and demanded that I go and get his autograph. At the time I had no idea who he was but he was a super nice guy to me.
Billy played for Wigan RLFC (my team) from 1953 - 1968 and still holds a scoring record to this day.
Statue of Billy in Wigan: Greater Manchester…although I still think of Wigan being a part of Lancashire (which it used to be)
He scored 478 tries in 488 matches for Wigan in the 1950s and 1960s. He became the most prolific British try-scorer in the history of the sport. He played 31 times for Great Britain and won the 1960 World Cup He was the first non-white player to join a Great Britain Lions tour in 1954. He broke racial barriers and fought against all kinds of racial prejudice during his career. RIP Billy Boston. FP Edit: Wow, Sir Billy and his family, I’m sure would be so happy to see this kind of appreciation mostly from (I’m guessing) people who have never before heard of him. It means a lot to me X

item.title: The Last Human - Love Languages [OC]
item.description:
Sauce: https://acrowdedgalaxy.com/read/YX6uD4aX9FZH
Bonus points to anyone who can tell me this potential victim's name.
https://ACrowdedGalaxy.com Fun fact: Widows generally don't go in for *attempted* murder. If a Widow wants you dead, there is very little you can do about it. But even the average Galactic citizen is absolutely capable of the *attempt*, if not the execution. How else would a species survive to First Contact, if not by fanatical protection of the next generation? --- The story so far (tl;dr): The comic was on hiatus because we were making it into a book, and the book is done. This week's episode: I don't know if you guys know how the publishing biz works. I don't even know if *I* know how the publishing biz works. But I can tell you how it's been for me: A daily grind of making stuff non-stop, in the crevices of time between day jobs and family, punctuated by a handful of events you'll remember for the rest of your life. The day I signed my first publishing contract was the best day of my life (top 5, at least). I would have signed away my soul. And then the next several years* were... hard. And yet, when someone offered me another contract, I said yes. And maybe it's not this way for some people. Maybe it's all joy, all the time. But for me, it feels like how I've heard childbirth described. I've been told that it's the hardest thing a person can go through. And then, as soon as they see the kid, those same people often decide to do it *again*. It's insanity. But anyway. That's my metaphor for signing up for more publishing contracts. So here's some news: Yesterday my partner on the comic called me (well, Discorded me). She told me she was ready to get back on the horse, so to speak. You guys have likely forgotten where this all came from, but the book is a rewrite of the first half of a much longer, mostly finished story arc. It's that "mostly" that has haunted us ever since we shifted to paper publishing, and many of you have given us (loving) hell for that decision. So in my conversation with Luyi, we decided that's what's up next: We're going to finish the arc online. Admittedly, this may not be as big a deal for you guys as it is for us, but I just wanted to share. Your friendly local killbot with a heart of gold and various other heavy metals, Zack (USKillbotics) --- * I sold my first two books, and this comic, as unfinished partials. This means that the last ten years of my life have been trying to deliver on promises I had no business making.
As always, if you can't support but still want to read, just make an account on https://ACrowdedGalaxy.com and I'll unlock the digital version for you.

item.title: Tim Curry trivia
item.description:
In memory of the prolific actor and icon Tim Curry (1946 - 2026), and among countless topics, this is a look at his professional rivalry and friendship with Ian McKellen.
Curry portrayed Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and McKellen his competitor Antonio Salieri when the new play Amadeus (1979) premiered on Broadway in 1980. During their time together on stage was Constanze Weber, the beloved of Mozart, at first portrayed by Jane Seymour (above) and later by Amy Irving.
In 1968 Curry was in the stage play Hair in London, and partied with McKellen due to shared social circles. Curry became known for The Rocky Horror Show in 1973, and on becoming co-stars in 1980 McKellen recalls on mckellen.com: “I had known Tim long before he struck stardom with the original stage production of Rocky Horror Picture Show. All in all I was looking forward to being back with old friends on Broadway...”
Curry in his memoir Vagabond (2025) wrote about their Broadway collaboration: “I liked him enough when we were acquaintances, though once we started Amadeus, our relationship became intensely competitive.”
“There were some strange points of jealousy and strain, and I suppose it’s accurate to say we had quite a rivalry while doing the play, and even a few confrontations—nothing physical, of course. We are both very British, so any discord between us was harmless. As a matter of fact, it ultimately provided valuable energy for the play.” (photo by Zoë Dominic).
“There was a legitimate rivalry between Mozart and Salieri. The tension between me and Ian made sense in the wider scheme of the plot and never distorted the performance. And that’s all that mattered to either of us.”
The role earned Curry his first Tony Award nomination in 1981, for ’Best Performance by a Leading Actor in a Play’, but he lost to McKellen. Though Curry in 2015 would call it his favourite stage production, both he and McKellen left for new work in 1981. Note: later Curry won ’Best Actor in a Musical’ for My Favorite Year (1992) and for Spamalot (2005).
The two actors were reunited, on the silver screen, in the comic book film The Shadow (1994). The official FB page Tim Curry News reports that Curry later shared: “It was terrific that he was doing The Shadow because we’d been friends for 20 years. We had a lot of fun on the set because we don’t take each other very seriously.”
They could even been reunited a second time; Crawley's Casting Calls reports on The Lord of the Rings (2001 - 2003) that if the primary choice for the wizard Saruman, Christopher Lee (1922 - 2015), had declined then director Peter Jackson considered actors as Tim Curry, Jeremy Irons, and Malcolm McDowell for the role (image by Geek Dave).

item.title: Bill Gates' thoughts on the future of AI
item.description:
WSource: Newser.com - https://www.newser.com/story/395317/bill-gates-issues-a-6k-word-ai-warning.html Link to the full essay on his website: https://www.gatesnotes.com/work/make-ai-work-for-everyone/reader/the-risks-of-ai-are-real-but-manageable
We don't like AI slop here on Imgur, but our opprobrium is most frequently heaved at AI-generated image and text. These thoughts don't even really touch on that, but are trying to cover the larger view.
Whatever you may think of Gates or his billions or his foundation or Microsoft, the man has a lifetime of experience in the computing world and is thinking cogently about potential effects on society as a whole.
My gut tells me that these are good and important points that must be added to the mix for consideration. Obviously other people than Bill have been thinking about this and sounding the alarm, but for good or ill, his voice has global reach and it's important to consider his thoughts. One thing he's right about for sure: we need a plan, toute de suite. Because every day that goes by, the tech bros and the billionaires *are* planning on how to monetize the hell out of AI, right now, and their plans sure as hell don't include you and me.
The prophet has spoken.
